name: Discovered attacks
goal: You can move one piece out of the way so that the piece behind it attacks, and use the moving piece to attack something else too.
intro: A discovered attack works like opening a door. One of your pieces stands in front of another on a line, and when the front piece moves, the piece behind it suddenly attacks. If the piece that moves makes a threat of its own, your opponent faces two attacks from a single move and usually cannot meet both.

parts.title: A blocked diagonal
parts.keyIdea: Move the front piece with a threat of its own, and the piece behind it attacks too: two threats with one move.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Your queen on f3 and Black's rook on a8 stand on the same long diagonal, but your pawn on c6 blocks the line between them.

notes.text: c7, the pawn one step forward, attacks Black's queen on d8 and knight on b8. At the same time it opens the diagonal, so your queen now attacks the rook on a8. Black cannot deal with all of that in one move.
Black took the pawn with the queen, but that does nothing for the rook on a8, which no black piece defends. Your queen takes it: you have won a rook for a pawn.

parts.title: Both rooks attacked
parts.keyIdea: Move the front piece to a square where it attacks the queen; while the queen escapes, the piece behind it captures what it attacks.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's knight has just jumped to d3, where it attacks both of your rooks. Your queen on d1 would like to take it, but your own knight on d2 is in the way.

notes.text: Ne4, the knight to e4, gets out of the way with a threat: from e4 it attacks Black's queen on f6. At the same time your queen on d1 now attacks the knight on d3. Black has to save the queen first.
Black's queen went to g7, and the knight on d3 still has no defender, so your queen takes it: you have won a piece, and your rooks are safe again.

parts.title: A bishop between two queens
parts.keyIdea: When the moving piece gives check, the opponent must answer it and has no time to save what the piece behind attacks.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are Black. White's queen has just moved to a6. Your bishop on d6 stands between your queen on f6 and White's queen.

notes.text: The bishop moves away with check, and your queen on f6 now attacks White's queen along the sixth rank. White has to answer the check first.
White took the bishop, but the queen on a6 is lost. Giving a bishop to win a queen is a very good trade.
